insights.headline: Gold sinks to 14-month low as Fed minutes point to more hikes
insights.summary: Spot gold fell 3.2% to $3,726 an ounce, its lowest since September 2025, and silver slid 5% to $45.03, after the Fed's October minutes showed most officials expect further rate hikes and Governor Waller raised a possible half-point December move. The dollar hit a 19-month high and Treasury yields climbed. In India, gold opened at Rs 1,31,505 per 10 g and silver at Rs 1,64,506 per kg, near one-year lows, and the rupee held at 93.44 per dollar. India's gold import bill could fall to $35–40 billion in FY27 from nearly $72 billion.
points: Spot gold fell 3.2% to $3,726 an ounce, its lowest since September 2025, after Fed minutes pointed to more rate hikes.
Silver slid 5% to $45.03 an ounce and platinum fell 4.1%, as the dollar hit a 19-month high and Treasury yields rose.
Indian gold opened at ₹1,31,505 per 10 g and silver at ₹1,64,506 per kg, with MCX December gold near ₹1,31,060 per 10 g.
India's gold import bill could fall to $35–40 billion in FY27 from nearly $72 billion, with imports down about 40% in April–October.
Markets price a 7.3% chance of a half-point Fed hike in December, up from 5.3% before the minutes were released.

brief.headline: Gold at 14-month low after hawkish Fed minutes
brief.summary: Spot gold fell 3.2% to $3,726 and MCX gold opened near Rs 1.31 lakh per 10 g as Fed minutes pointed to more rate hikes.

bullets.text: Fed minutes showed almost all officials saw more hikes ahead, and Governor Waller raised a possible half-point December move.
The rupee stayed at 93.44 per dollar as FII inflows offset importer demand, while MCX gold tracked the global slide.
Next on the calendar: the Fed's December 8-9 meeting, with markets pricing about a 95% chance of a hike.

trending.title: Fed hike bets hammer bullion to 14-month lows
trending.summary: Gold fell 3.2% to $3,726 and silver 5% to $45.03 as the Fed's October minutes and Waller's half-point hint lifted the dollar to a 19-month high and pushed yields up.

trending.title: Silver's slide deepens toward $45 support
trending.summary: Silver has fallen nearly 12% in five sessions to about $45, with traders watching $45 as the key level; in India the sharp correction is drawing buyers back for coins and bars.

trending.title: India's gold import bill is shrinking fast
trending.summary: Higher duty has cut gold imports about 40% in April-October, and the FY27 bill could fall to $35-40 billion from nearly $72 billion, though October imports tripled from September.

trending.title: Rupee holds near seven-month high on inflows
trending.summary: The rupee closed at 93.44 per dollar, broadly steady, as foreign fund inflows offset dollar buying by public-sector banks for importers.

trending.title: Correction hits jewellers, financiers and demand
trending.summary: Titan, Kalyan and gold financiers fell as prices corrected, while jewellers say buyers are returning for smaller purchases and the wedding season may support demand.

items.title: Gold drops to 14-month low as dollar, yields rise on hawkish Fed rhetoric
items.summary: Spot gold sank 3.2% to $3,726 an ounce, its lowest since September 2025, after the Fed's October minutes showed most officials see further rate hikes and Governor Waller backed a possible half-point December rise. US gold futures settled at $3,741.90, silver slid 5% to $45.03 and platinum fell 4.1%, as the dollar hit a 19-month high.

items.title: Gold plunges below $3,750, silver tumbles as hawkish Fed minutes pressure metals
items.summary: Spot gold fell 3.3% to $3,722.60 an ounce, its lowest since September 2025, and silver slid 5% to $44.93 after the Fed's October minutes reinforced expectations of more rate hikes. Governor Waller raised a possible half-point December move, the dollar held near a 19-month high and the 10-year yield stayed above 5%, while US housing data pointed to weakness.

Indian gold and silver fell to their lowest in a year, tracking the slide. IBJA data showed gold opening at Rs 1,31,505 per 10 g and silver at Rs 1,64,506 per kg; spot gold was $3,772 at 13:00 IST and silver $45.90. MCX December gold stood at Rs 1,31,060 per 10 g. Gold has shed about Rs 10,000 per 10 g since November began, and traders await the Fed's October minutes, due 00:30 IST Thursday.
items.title: Gold, silver prices in Indian markets crash to nearly a year's low
Gold and silver 'can't find a floor' as Waller calls for Fed rate hike
items.summary: Gold fell towards $3,744, as much as 3.6% below last Friday's finish, and silver dropped near $45 an ounce after Fed Governor Christopher Waller suggested a 50-basis-point rate hike in December. Silver fixed around $45.90 at London's midday auction, and BullionVault called it gold's worst stretch of weekly losses since 1989, with January hike odds in Fed futures already above 70%.

items.title: Gold slumps below $3,800 as Fed officials signal more rate hikes
items.summary: Spot gold fell 1.4% to $3,795.55 an ounce, below $3,800 for the first time since September 2025, after Fed officials made the case for more rate hikes. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the US economy would likely need several rate increases before spring. Silver dropped 2.6% to $46.18 an ounce. Investors await the Fed's October meeting minutes, due later Wednesday.

items.title: Gold slides to over one-year low on firm dollar, US rate outlook
items.summary: Spot gold fell 1.4% to $3,796.37, its lowest since September 2025, as a firm dollar near a 19-month high and expectations of higher US rates weighed; silver slipped 2.9% to $46.01. Markets price a 95.7% chance of a December Fed hike, and await the minutes of the Fed's October meeting due at 1900 GMT.

items.title: $32 Billion Squeeze: Why India's Massive Gold Import Bill Is Shrinking Fast
items.summary: India's gold import bill could fall to $35-40 billion in FY27 from nearly $72 billion in FY26, NDTV Profit reports, with gold imports down about 40% to $24.78 billion in April-October. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal attributed the fall to the higher customs duty introduced in May, which made overseas purchases more expensive.

items.title: Gold and silver weather a perfect storm as demand holds firm
items.summary: Gold fell 6.8% in October to $3,874.62 an ounce, a 52-week low, and silver slid 18.7%, but the drop looked like a positioning and liquidity reset rather than weakening demand, Sprott says: gold ETF holdings rose to 100.97 million ounces and silver ETF holdings also recovered, while Chinese physical buying absorbed Western selling.

items.title: Gold, silver divide widens: Why SLV looks riskier than GLD as Fed rate fears mount
items.summary: The gold-silver ratio climbed to a one-year high of 82.6 as silver fell harder than gold, Benzinga reports: December gold futures fell 2.34% to $3,773.80 an ounce while silver futures dropped 2.45% to $45.68. Gold ETF GLD fell 2.4% and silver ETF SLV slid 4.4% on Wednesday morning, both touching their lowest since September 2025, with markets pricing a 96.4% chance of a December Fed hike.

items.title: Silver analysis: XAG/USD continues to set new lows for the year
items.summary: Silver has fallen nearly 12% over the last five trading sessions, FOREX.com notes, with US 10-year Treasury yields holding above 5.0%. Traders are watching $45 as critical support, lows not seen since October 2025, with $49 as a nearby barrier and $54 as resistance.

items.title: Silver Bears Eye $35: At That Price, 1-Kg Silver May Cost Less Than 10 Gm Of Gold In India
items.summary: Technical analysts warn silver could slide towards $35 an ounce; with gold near $3,765, that would lift the gold-silver ratio to its highest since 2020 and make 1 kg of silver cheaper than 10 gm of gold on MCX.

items.title: India Rupee Review: Steady as FII inflows offset importers' dollar demand
items.summary: The rupee ended broadly steady at 93.44 per dollar on Wednesday, after opening at 93.4050, as foreign institutional inflows offset dollar purchases by public-sector banks for importers. The currency had touched a seven-month high in early trade before giving back gains as the dollar strengthened. Dealers said RBI maturities in the non-deliverable forward market also weighed.

items.title: Gold Imports Triple In October To $5.51 Billion, But Remain Well Below Historical Levels
items.summary: India's gold imports more than tripled in October to $5.51 billion from September, but were 63% lower than a year earlier; the World Gold Council attributes the gap to unofficial supplies and recycled gold despite healthy Dhanteras-Diwali demand.

items.title: Central banks rethink gold as global risks mount
items.summary: Central banks are increasingly weighing geopolitical uncertainty alongside traditional financial risks when managing gold reserves, according to a new OMFIF report, while tokenization and retail investors reshape how gold is held and traded.

items.title: US 10-Year Yield Set for Historic Run Above 5% on Fed Cycle
items.summary: The US 10-year Treasury yield is on pace for its 27th close above 5% in 2026, near the 29 of 2007, after hotter October inflation pushed traders to fully price a quarter-point Fed hike on December 9 and over 80 basis points of tightening by September 2027. The yield traded near 5.09% on Tuesday; JPMorgan's Priya Misra tied yields over 5% to a risk premium from uncertainty about the Fed.

items.title: Gold struggles near one-year lows, silver rebounds as stocks slide, Fed hike bets persist - Kitco PM Report
items.summary: Spot gold held near $3,853 in late US trading on Tuesday, just above Monday's 13-month low, while silver rebounded about 1% to $47.33 on bargain hunting. Weaker US data, lower yields and fresh geopolitical tensions competed with near-certain bets on a December Fed hike, and equities fell again. Traders now await US housing data and the Fed's October minutes on Wednesday.

items.title: Silver's sharp correction brings buyers back to the market
items.summary: Silver's steep correction — down nearly 57% to about ₹1.7 lakh per kg from January's ₹4 lakh record — is bringing buyers back for coins, bars and smaller denominations, jewellers say, with staggered purchases rather than bulk buying. Augmont's Renisha Chainani expects silver to consolidate between $44 and $53 an ounce; the gold-silver ratio is around 82, up from about 46 at January's peak.

items.title: Silver Is Paying for a Rate Rise That Has Not Happened Yet
items.summary: Silver lost about 11% in a week, against 6% for gold, because the cost of money is rising, not because silver's supply shortfall has ended, FXEmpire argues. A hot October US inflation report pushed markets to treat a December Fed rate rise as close to certain; silver traded near $47.24. Metals Focus and the Silver Institute still forecast a sixth straight annual deficit.

items.title: Gold financiers under pressure; Muthoot, Manappuram fall 5%; here's why
items.summary: Shares of gold lenders Muthoot Finance and Manappuram Finance fell about 5% as gold slid below $3,800 to a one-year low. Analysts say falling prices could strain gold-loan books as the value of pledged gold drops, with lenders that rolled old loans into fresh ones seen as most exposed.

items.title: Gold prices slide sharply: What does the correction mean for Titan, Kalyan Jewellers and gold financiers?
items.summary: Gold fell for a sixth straight session in Delhi while silver crashed 5.3% to Rs 1,69,500 per kg, a one-year low. Shares of gold lenders Muthoot Finance and Manappuram Finance fell more than 3% on the slide, while IIFL Finance rose 5.5%.

items.title: As Gold Stays Costly, Indians Are Rethinking What They Buy and How Much
items.summary: World Gold Council data shows India's gold demand fell 29% to 162.5 tonnes in July-September even as its value rose 3% to Rs 2.42 lakh crore, with jewellery volumes down 20% while spending rose 16%, a rise the WGC called entirely price-led. Buyers are choosing lighter, lower-carat jewellery and exchanging old gold; Dhanteras sales were put at about Rs 60,000 crore, up 15-20% with quantity flat.

items.title: Gold price correction may support jewellery demand during India's wedding season: WGC
items.summary: The World Gold Council says lower gold prices and the ongoing wedding season should support jewellery demand in India, though a sharp rise could temper buying. Festive demand stayed healthy through Dhanteras and Diwali, with demand in value terms up 15-25% year on year. International gold fell 6.3% in October to $3,913 an ounce, and domestic gold has corrected more than 15% over three months.

items.title: India gold market update: Gold demand gets festive boost
items.summary: The World Gold Council says festive demand was healthy across regions in jewellery and bars and coins, helped by softer prices; Indian gold ETFs saw a fifth straight month of net inflows in October at Rs 35bn, imports rebounded to a six-month high, and domestic discounts narrowed to $5/oz by 12 November.

items.title: China gold market update: Robust demand in October
items.summary: China's central bank stretched its gold-buying streak to 24 months with its largest monthly addition since late 2023, adding 25.8 tonnes in October, the World Gold Council says; Chinese gold ETFs drew inflows for a fourth straight month to another record, and Shanghai Gold Exchange withdrawals rose month on month.

items.title: SEBI revises minimum margin norms for commodity derivatives
items.summary: SEBI has revised minimum initial margins for commodity derivatives to 6% for low-volatility, 8% for medium and 10% for high-volatility contracts, applying uniformly to agricultural and non-agricultural commodities including bullion, with margin periods of risk of two to three days. The norms take effect on December 1, 2026 for one year.

items.title: RBI announces premature redemption rate for Sovereign Gold Bonds due November 18
items.summary: RBI has fixed the premature redemption price for Sovereign Gold Bond 2020-21 Series VIII at ₹13,499 per unit for redemption on November 18, 2026, based on the simple average of IBJA 999-purity gold closing prices on November 13, 16 and 17. The tranche was issued on November 18, 2020 at ₹5,127 per gram for online investors.
